Karamjit Singh, J. (Oral)
1. Prayer in the present civil revision petition is for issuance of direction to reference Court-cum-Additional District Judge, Sangrur for expeditious disposal of execution petition bearing No.1161-2019 titled Jagjit Singh and others Vs. State of Punjab.
opennyai_summary.13_August_2024__facts: Thereupon, the petitioner and other land owners filed execution application in year 2019 and the same is pending since then and till date, the enhanced amount of compensation is not disbursed to the petitioner and other land owners.
opennyai_summary.13_August_2024__ANALYSIS:
In Rahul S. Shah Vs. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi and others (2021) 6 SCC 418, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follow:-
"That the executing Court must dispose of execution proceeding within 6 months from the date of filing which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay."
7.
opennyai_summary.13_August_2024__decision:
In view of the above, the Court of Additional District Judge, Sangrur (the Executing Court) is requested to dispose of the execution petition bearing No.1161-2019 as expeditiously as possible,
preferably within a period of next 3 months from today, as the further delay is going to cause serious prejudice to the rights of the petitioner-land owner.
8. It is made clear that nothing said herein-above shall be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the execution proceedings.
9.
The present petition is disposed of in aforesaid terms.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
2. Admittedly, certain land owned by the petitioner was acquired vide notifications dated 20.11.2006 and 29.04.2007, .04.2007, issued under Sections 4 and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (in short '1894 Act') respectively, followed by an award dated 12.04.2008, whereby, the petitioner and other persons were granted granted compensation to the tune of Rs.6 lacs per acre including solatium for land of nine villages at flat rate and Rs.10 lacs per acre for the land acquired of the village Khanauri.
3. Feeling dissatisfied, the land owners filed petition under Section 18 of the Act, which was dismissed by the reference Court vide award dated 15.12.2010.
Thereafter, the land owners challenged the said award before this Court by way of bunch of appeals seeking enhancement of compensation and the same were allowed while enhancing the market value to the tune of Rs.15,95,600/- per acre for the acquired land of nine villages and Rs.21 lac per acre was enhanced at the uniform rate as regards village Khanauri, vide decision dated 27.1.2016 (Annexure P-1).
Thereafter, the judgment debtor made part payment under the award to the decree holder/petitioner except solatium and interest thereof, pursuant to the order dated 27.02.2017 passed by the Additional District Judge, Sangrur and the same was challenged before this Court in CR-4676-2017, which was disposed of vide order dated 21.07.2017, whereby directions were issued to decide the objections filed by the JDs, afresh.
Thereafter, the petitioner and other land owners filed execution application No.1162 of 2019 and the same is pending since then and till date,
the enhanced amount of compensation has not been disbursed to the petitioner and other land owners.
6. A perusal of record shows that execution application (Annexure P-5) filed by the petitioner and other land owners on 29.07.2019, is still pending and the petitioner is waiting to get his amount of compensation on the basis of order dated 27.01.2016 and order dated 21.07.2017.
7.
opennyai_summary.arguments: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner being aggrieved of the non-disbursal of amount of compensation has filed the present revision petition for issuance of direction to the Executing Court concerned to decide the execution application expeditiously, in a time bound manner.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
In "Rahul S. Shah Vs. Jinendra Kumar Gandhi and others (2021) 6 SCC 418", the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follow:-
"That the executing Court must dispose of execution proceeding within 6 months from the date of filing which may be extended only by recording reasons in writing for such delay."
8.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
In view of the above, the Court of Additional District Judge, Sangrur (the Executing Court) is requested to dispose of the execution petition bearing No.1162-2019 as expeditiously as possible,
preferably within a period of next 3 months from today, as any further delay is going to cause serious prejudice to the rights of the petitioner-land owner.
9. It is made clear that nothing said herein-above shall be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the execution proceedings.
10. The present petition is disposed of in aforesaid terms.
